pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 10.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: how the events in the short story relate to real life. 1. How do events flow logically in a story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the setting in the short story

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify the setting in the short story
   In simple words: practise until you can identify the setting in the short story. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story.
4. Show that you can: identify the setting in the short story

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss with peers the main events,
2. Discuss the setting of the short story they have read,
3. Communication and collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner discusses with peers the main events and how they relate to real life.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how the events in the short story relate to real life. 1. How do events flow logically in a story?
2. Why is the setting of a story important to the reader?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the setting in the short story

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
